title: Order-Preserving Cryptography for the Confidential Inference in Random Forests: FPGA Design and Implementation
problem: Scaling order-preserving encryption for confidential inference from individual decision trees to random forest ensembles while managing tradeoffs between encryption strength, classification accuracy, and edge platform resource constraints.
motivation: Random forests significantly outperform individual decision trees in classification accuracy, but enabling confidential inference on encrypted data at the edge requires efficient cryptographic implementations on resource-constrained FPGA platforms.
method: The paper develops a methodology and FPGA implementation strategy for scaling order-preserving encryption (OPE) to random forests. It uses a framework to systematically analyze multifaceted tradeoffs between the number of trees in the forest, encryption strength, inference accuracy, and available FPGA resources. The approach is implemented and validated on Intel DE10 Standard FPGA board using MNIST dataset.
key_novelty: FPGA-based implementation framework for scaling order-preserving cryptography from single decision trees to random forest ensembles with explicit multi-dimensional tradeoff analysis.
contributions: FPGA implementation methodology for confidential inference on random forests using order-preserving encryption
Framework for analyzing tradeoffs between encryption strength, classification accuracy, forest size, and FPGA resource consumption
Empirical validation and resource characterization on Intel DE10 Standard edge platform
Demonstration of scalability from individual decision trees to multi-tree ensembles

metrics.other: Encryption strength vs. FPGA resources vs. inference accuracy tradeoffs

limitations: Specific implementation bottlenecks, scalability limits, and generalization to other datasets not discussed.
primary_theme: Secure tree ensemble inference on edge devices
